posts.author: Garryg
posts.body:
Ok I've basically been working on Three games in different versions of RPG Maker (on and off) in the past.
And if I've realised anything it's that I'm way more interested in making mechanics in the Engines than making the actual games.
After I make an interesting mechanic work I tend to loose interest in the drudgery of actually finishing a coherent game.
Although I do intent to finish the two games I'm still working on.
One is done in XP and just needs some polish and a few more story elements to make it more coherent. The other is using MV and basically at the 'testing the mechanics' stage just now (falling, jumping, bitmap manipulation, etc - the normal stuff). None of these are likely to be hits in the RPG Makes gaming space!
Right now my plan is to make three small demo games, just because I find the concepts interesting:
1) TITLE: The mirror realm.
A short proof of concept demo where the screen is mirrored with the action being repeated on both sides.
And switching when the player crosses over a 'mirror' line.
- To play around with automating screen rendering.
2) TITLE: Dicing with death.
A short proof of concept game for a dice based battle mechanic.
Whare random on map encounters and the battle system use dice roles.
- To practice injecting custom logic into the movement and battle core game loops.
3) TITLE: The Illusion of Depth
An isometric perspective game on RPG Maker, where the player can walk behind and in front of isometric objects.
This would need to include isometric scrolling.
- To play around with the coordinates and tile priority systems (surprisingly still there under the hood in MV)
Nobody will probably bother with these much as they will all be written on XP; I can concentrate on the code without fighting the plugin system there.
The thing is most people seem to be on MZ. So once these XP demos are done would anybody be interested in plugins that add this type of functionality. Bearing in mind that plugins are inherently more limiting that the XP scripting process! I've made a start on Plugins with MV.
I've been a professional programmer for years and RPG Maker is a hobby to me, but I like tinkering with it.

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
I totally get this. I actually love experimenting with ideas and mechanics to get them to work. To me, that is much more enjoyable than the other parts of putting a game together.
Many of my experiments start with "Can I do this?" or "Can I make something like that work?" or "How would I actually do that?" or "You know what, I think I know how to recreate that!"
I'm sure many people would love having more options for plugins.
But another thing to consider is that there are many people who would also enjoy learning how you made the mechanics work, especially if you did things without plugins.
Have you considered making tutorials about mechanics or tutorials about how you made a plugin?
I know that I greatly appreciate tutorials as a way of increasing my knowledge of RPG Maker.
Good luck on your projects!

posts.author: Garryg
posts.body:
I could do that. I've wrote many user manuals and technical specs as part of my day job over the years! I'm not really focused on 'making scripts for people' but I would be happy to explain what I've done with a small example to learn people how to make simple scrips themselves. I know it's not what the majority of users want. But after decades I'm stuck with 'programmers brain' now
There are a lot more 'tricks' in my 'Hauntly Hall' game than first appears. The game is there but it was more a learning experience about screen formatting and using bitmaps etc...
By the way, for anybody having a quick look at that one my graphics tend to be, um, unique! This one was meant to have that old CGA feel. Something that may not translate well to a 'modern audience'

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
There are a lot of users like this, especially plugin devs it seems, who have tons of plugins under their name but no finished games to speak of. I have several playable tech demos (made in another engine) that I share with people when they ask what I'm working on to demonstrate a certain type of gameplay but haven't fleshed them out into full games yet.
Sadly can't share them here but I've been having fun doing mechanics I could never make in RPG Maker, especially 3D games.
If you're making scripts in XP the Pokemon fangame community might be interested since they're the biggest users of XP due to Pokemon Essentials

posts.author: Garryg
posts.body: Yes I've heard of the Pokemon Essentials, it should be interesting to see what was done at the script level there. I do try to make games that are 'finished' at least in my eyes. But I've never made a 'normal' RPG Maker game. What initially interested me in the platform was the old horror games that were made with it, not any actual RPG games. Maybe I'll make the 'Ant Attack' essentials pack. For all those people who want to make Ant Attack clones
